notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

RPG Maker XP, VX and VX Ace games run natively in PC Games. Add the game's folder on the web page like any PC game: SCCM Retro sees that it is an RPG Maker game and runs it with mkxp-z instead of as a Windows program, full screen, with the controller (A confirms, B cancels, X or Plus opens the menu, Y runs in many games). If a game does not work that way, set RPG Maker player to Windows in its menu. Many games need RPG Maker's RTP, its shared graphics and sounds, which SCCM Retro cannot include: install it on a computer (a free download from rpgmakerweb.com) and copy its folder (for example Standard) to SCCM-Retro/bios/rpgmaker on the SD card. A game that stops for a missing RTP file closes and says which one. MIDI music plays only with a SoundFont (.sf2) in that same folder.

Installing SCCM Retro with the SCCM Retro app: the install could stop on hekate's logo on some SD cards (FAT32 cards not formatted by hekate). The app's installer reads its files in small pieces again, as it did from 2.42.36, so those cards install. The app is updated on consoles and on the download page.

DOS games: a zip with a disk image inside (an .img, for example) is no longer split up. The whole zip goes to Unsorted with DOS suggested, and when it starts, DOSBox Pure offers both the disk image and the game's programs.

When a PC game needs its program chosen first, the message now shows the web page's address.

On Stable releases only, checking for updates now tells you when Latest Updates has a newer version, instead of just saying you are up to date.

The debug report includes more about controllers and per-game audio, to help with two Joy-Con pairs and silent PS2 games.

New and lightly tested: RPG Maker support was checked with test games made for it, not a real RPG Maker game yet. The installer fix was checked against the earlier fix's own files and the app's tests, not with a real install on an affected card.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
